elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 4.1: "unless terminated by either Party hereto at any time upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other", read with "Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated" — the Company may end the Agreement without cause (no Order Form structure exists in this hosting agreement).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Notice period remains "ninety (90) days written notice"; no 30-day notice was inserted.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere; on the contrary, Company termination triggers a Termination Payment to HDI under 4.1(a), now merely capped.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Any termination by HDI under this Section 4.1 shall be effective only at the end of the then-current term, and any Termination Date specified in HDI's notice shall be the last day of that term." HDI therefore cannot exit mid-term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "terminated by either Party hereto at any time upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 band, and the inserted "at any time" (plus the retained sentence allowing the notice to fix any Termination Date) converts what could be read as a non-renewal mechanic into an operative mid-term convenience right. The deterministic 'Customer convenience termination present' regex is false only because the clause does not use the words "Company may terminate ... for convenience"; in substance the right is unconditional and no-cause.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "In no event shall the Termination Payment exceed the amounts payable by the Company to HDI under Section 3 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." The uncapped Net-Sales formula in 4.1(a) and the eight-instalment mechanic in 4.1(c) survive but are ceilinged at three months of the Section 3 consideration.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence expressly ties the effective date of any HDI termination under Section 4.1 to "the end of the then-current term" and conforms the Termination Date, satisfying the requirement that the effective date, not just the notice, be term-end anchored.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Already met by retained text: "upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other", which applies to either Party including HDI.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: Customer convenience exit at 90 days, HDI limited to term-end termination with 90 days' notice, and the Termination Payment capped at three months of Section 3 amounts.

Preferred level fails on two elements — the notice period stays at 90 days rather than 30, and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (the clause runs the other way, with a payment from Company to HDI). These are correctly treated as accepted shortfalls given the fallback is reached.

Minimality holds: three surgical edits (a two-word "at any time" clarifier, one HDI term-end sentence, one cap sentence), no deletions, no survival tails, no expense or damages extras, and the existing 90-day notice and instalment mechanics are retained rather than rewritten. The trailing words "and any Termination Date specified in HDI's notice shall be the last day of that term" are justified because they conform the retained "Such notice shall specify the date" sentence and prevent a contradictory retained mechanic.

Intent is preserved: the Net Sales formula, the $800,000 deduction, the divide-by-two mechanic and the eight quarterly instalments all survive, subject only to the new ceiling; no term is left undefined by the edits and the HDI limit is scoped to Section 4.1 so any for-cause termination rights elsewhere are untouched.

Residual drafting risk to tighten if the counterparty pushes back: the cap depends on "amounts payable by the Company to HDI under Section 3" — Section 3 is not among the cited paragraphs, so confirm it is in fact the fee/revenue-share section and that amounts run from Company to HDI; if the flow is reversed or Section 3 is silent, the cap could be read as nil or undefined. Consider "the fees payable by the Company to HDI under Section 3 (or, if none, the amounts otherwise payable by the Company under this Agreement) for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date".

Optional hardening of element 1: because the Company's right still sits grammatically inside the auto-renewal sentence, a cleaner formulation would be a standalone sentence — "Either Party may terminate this Agreement at any time, with or without cause, upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice" — but the current "at any time" insertion read with the Termination Date sentence is sufficient in substance.
